decisions.reason: The interval-additivity statement does not supply integrand linearity, but the existing vector-integral Definition explicitly does. Corrected its attribution and supplied constant integration; the periodic extension and averaging datum retain exactly the same values and hypotheses. Joint continuity on compact products is now justified by an explicit uniform integral estimate.

The original x_j formula divides by zero at j=0 under the library natural-number convention. Replaced j by j+1, yielding interior points for every j in N and the same boundary limit. FTC plus coordinatewise zero-derivative constancy explicitly identifies the periodic extension with the oriented integral for all real t; compact-rectangle differentiation and the unit-vector integral estimates establish the unchanged derivative and norm bounds. Owning contract synchronization is pending the shared write lock.

The primitive corollary states its evaluation clause for a<t. F5 previously attributed the arbitrary-order version to that clause alone, although step 1.2 allows t<a. Added the oriented-integral Definition and explicitly derived reversed and equal endpoint cases. Integrating-factor classification, coefficient uniqueness, opposite-sign roots and exponential limits remain valid with unchanged Statement. Contract synchronization is pending the shared write lock.

L2 cited integrability of a composite as continuity of a composite. Replaced that supplier with thm-composition-of-continuous-functions, whose exact domain condition holds for abs:R->[0,infinity) and sqrt on [0,infinity). Explicit square-root existence and square monotonicity establish the continuous inverse hypotheses. Removed the unused unsupported sqrt derivative assertion; the delayed quadratic is differentiable at its join and satisfies the ODE by nonnegative-root uniqueness. The refuted Statement is unchanged.

The root comparison in step 1.1 needs monotonicity of exp, absent from the cited limits/range interface. Added thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing with its exact order consequence, and cited positivity/reciprocity for the critical-damping series bound. Negative exponents and bounded trig factors give the other two estimates; t exp(lambda t)<=2/(lambda^2 t) proves critical decay. All stated bounds and hypotheses remain unchanged.

The sequence t_k reused the fixed real spring parameter and specified only k>=0; integer periodicity did not justify that indexing. Replaced it with an explicit j in N sequence tending to infinity and retained f0!=0. Defined amplitude as sup_R |u| before use and verified the claimed value by the Pythagorean identity and an attained phase, including Omega=0 and f0=0. Cited the exact trig range/identity facts for boundedness; differentiated responses and homogeneous transient decay remain valid. Statement unchanged.

The original suppliers established derivatives and the pi bound but did not state cosine periodicity or sin(2pi)=0. Added the exact zero-set/period theorem and trig range theorem. Step 1.1 now verifies continuity, periodicity, the state derivative, and M=1,L=0; endpoint sine zeros justify bar f=0 and g=sin t. The trapped y=0, strict pi/25<1/2 and exact x=sin t/100 establish the unchanged example on [0,100].

L1 omitted the linearization theorem domain, continuity, state-local-Lipschitz, and positive datum/horizon hypotheses. Restored those exact assumptions and proved ||F(z)-F(w)||<=||z-w|| globally by MVT, with U=R^2 containing the trapping ball. The sine Taylor regularity and constant-integral premise are explicit. Remainder C=1/12, L=||A||=1, delta=1/100, strict e/100<1/2, and the positive majorant integral still yield error <=3/4 times 10^-4<10^-4. Example unchanged. Added the L1 trailing tag to step 1.2 to match its explicit theorem-hypothesis check and the exact proof-contract input.

The proof announcement incorrectly called sqrt decreasing, while F3 and step 3.1 correctly use its increase and reciprocal decrease. Corrected that sentence and explicitly cited nonnegative-root existence. Completing q(u) square, the derivative 4m^2 Omega(Omega^2-u*) and positive denominator prove both strict branches and the unique peak, including u*=0. The undamped remark now describes the diverging quarter-turn values precisely. Statement and peak formula are unchanged.

The remark asserted an unbounded resonant solution without the supplier condition f0!=0. At f0=0 its displayed xp=f0 t sin(omega0 t)/(2m omega0) is identically zero, a concrete counterexample to that assertion. Restored the nonzero-drive condition and explicitly described zero drive; also retained f0!=0 for the amplitude maximum and undamped singular-frequency limit. The finite-time, averaging trapping, and adiabatic chart/frequency qualifications agree with the exact suppliers. No Statement/Definition or physical interface changed.
